job.title: A house on Waiheke Island
job.what: A proposed two-bedroom house on piles with a mono-pitch roof. A design study from draft drawings, not a record of anything built.
job.drawings: Draft set printed 17 November 2026: ground floor plan RC-031, site sheets RC-030 and RC-014, elevations and section RC-020, area plans RC-016, 3D sketch RC-029.
job.permission: Shown in the lab with the owner's permission. The address is not recorded here.
job.taken: Walls, openings, rooms, decks, roof overhangs, the entry stair and the car bay scaled from the 17 November 2026 sheets (the floor plan carries no written dimensions; scaled figures are good to about 20 mm). Checked against those sheets on 21 November 2026: layout and openings within about 30 mm. Window and door heights from the elevations. Landing levels, materials and the door detail are assumed.
job.site: Ground from the LINZ 1 m LiDAR, aerial photo from LINZ 0.075 m imagery (Auckland 2024), parcel boundary from LINZ primary parcels; all CC BY 4.0. Floor level set from the section (ground about 0.8 m above the floor at the uphill wall). Trees placed and sized from the LiDAR canopy; species not identified.

units: Metres. x east, z south, y up. Inside a building: u and v from its corner. The plan is turned a quarter turn from the drawing sheet: sheet-up is +u here.

changes: First reading from the draft partial set, for checking against the architect's model

terrain.source: LINZ 1 m LiDAR ground and surface models (Auckland 2024) and 0.075 m aerial photo (Auckland 2024), CC BY 4.0. Trees placed and sized from the surface model minus the ground. The house platform and a view corridor downhill are shown cleared; that clearing is proposed, not surveyed.

clearing.note: Proposed clearing for the house, inside the site boundary only: open ground round the house and decks, the view corridor downhill and a gap for morning sun to the east deck. Surveyed trees inside these areas are left out of the model, apart from the specimens kept. The survey's own list of trees is unchanged, and the bush beyond the boundary is shown as surveyed.
